details: CONFIRMED by reproduction. _stop_at_limit runs stop_tree once: it lists the descendants, SIGTERMs them, waits up to STOP_GRACE,
then SIGKILLs the list plus whatever is below at that moment. Nothing stops the step function itself: step() only raises
_LimitStop after fn returns. Any step that runs several programs in a row keeps going after the kill: validate_all loops over
`.` and every plugin folder (9 today), rules_tests runs three programs (it returns early on the first non-zero, so it is safe),
hook_tests on the full path runs more. A hung `claude plugin validate` (the claude CLI waiting on network or auth) hangs every
call, so the gate the limit exists to bound runs forever, the failure the queue item names. The same one-shot design leaves a
tiny race: if the timer fires between step()'s `if self.stopped` check and the child's Popen, stopped_step is set (or "")
and the child starts after the last listing, unkilled.
Size: 15 agent minutes.
evidence: $ python3 scratchpad/probe/validate_hang.py <worktree>/lib     (limit 2 s, fake claude = exec sleep 600, plugins a b c)
STILL RUNNING after 25 s (limit 2 s) None 25.0
lib/relay_ci.py:485-490 _stop_at_limit: one stop_tree(_descendants(me), me), then the thread ends.
lib/relay_ci.py:278-301 step(): _LimitStop only after fn(log) returns.
failing_case: Quick Ci, RELAY_CI_QUICK_LIMIT=2, plugins/a, plugins/b, plugins/c in the root, a `claude` on PATH that runs `sleep 600`
(a hung `claude plugin validate`), every other step stubbed to 0. Now: the watchdog at 2 s kills the validate of `.` and the
one started during the grace (plugins/a), then validate_all's loop starts plugins/b, which nobody kills: main() has not
returned after 25 s and would not before 600 s per dir. Should: main() returns 124 within limit + STOP_GRACE + a few seconds,
with "gate: stopped at the 2-second limit, step plugin validate was running".
fix_hint: In Ci.run, once self.stopped is set, start nothing: write "stopped at the time limit: <argv[0]> not started" to the log and
return CompletedProcess(argv, LIMIT_EXIT). That ends validate_all's loop at once (each later call returns at once) and closes
the step-start race except for the few bytecodes between the check and Popen; for those, the watchdog can stop the tree a
second time after a short sleep, or step() can check self.stopped after setting self.running.
pass_cases: 1. The failing case above: main() returns 124 in under 15 s; results.txt has "plugin validate STOPPED"; no `sleep 600` below the test process is left.
2. A step fn that calls ci.run twice, each a `sleep 600` (limit 2 s): main() returns 124 in under 15 s (the second program is never started or is killed).
3. T1 as today: one child plus a grandchild, both gone, 124, the exact line.
4. T2 as today: a normal 0.1 s run with limit 3 s is green, exit 0, no Timer alive after main().
reason: tests/test_ci_python.py:407 and :421 pass; :421 fails on base. Loop test bounded at 15 s, fixer saw it hang unfixed.
findings.summary: the watchdog kills only once: a step that starts another program after the kill (plugin validate's loop) runs unbounded

details: CONFIRMED by reading. relay_land._locked maps relay_gate.LIMIT_EXIT to HANDED_BACK on every run with no look at earlier logs;
relay_gate.finished_red skips exit 124, so every land runs the gate again; plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md:128 turns
exit 4 into "run it again". The existing HANDED_BACK causes (default branch moved, index.lock held) are transient; a stop may
not be (no per-test timeout in tests/parallel_unittest.py: grep finds only timeout=60 on helper calls). This is a wait with
no bound, and it costs a gate slot (2 on 12 cores) for 30 min each round. The design decided "handed back, not red" for a
stop (owner can reverse); a bound on a repeat stop fits inside that decision: the first stop is still handed back.
The state is derivable (principle 3): the committed <sha>.gate.log of the same code ending "exit 124".
Size: 20 agent minutes.
evidence: lib/relay_land.py:346-349: if code == relay_gate.LIMIT_EXIT: raise Stop(HANDED_BACK, [... "relay land {branch} again"])
lib/relay_gate.py:289: finished_red ... and int(last[1]) != LIMIT_EXIT  (a stopped log is never reused)
plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md:128: "Exit 4 handed back: run it again."
plugins/delegate/workflows/cycle.js:143-147: the cycle stops after gate_reruns; land has no such count.
failing_case: A branch whose merged code has a test that deadlocks (it hangs on every run). `relay land wt/x`: the gate stops at 30 min,
exit 4 "relay land wt/x again"; the front skill says "Exit 4 handed back: run it again", so it runs it again: stopped again,
exit 4, and so on, 30 min of a gate slot each time, never a fixer and never the owner. The cycle bounds the same case
(gate_reruns, default 1, then the unit stops with the line); land does not. Should: the second stop on the same code is not
"run it again" (red with the stopped line, or a refusal that names the step and sends it to a fix unit or the owner).
fix_hint: Before the gate (or on a 124), walk the same code's logs as finished_red does (only .relay/checks commits between) for one
ending "exit 124" with the same cmd; when one exists, this is the second stop: raise Stop(RED, ["land: the gate of <branch>
stopped at the limit twice on the same code (step <name>): a hang, not load", ...]) so the front sends a fix unit. Or a
refusal with that line; either keeps the first stop as handed back.
pass_cases: 1. Gate stub exits 124 on every run: the first `relay land wt/x` exits 4 with "relay land wt/x again"; the second on the same code exits non-4 (1 or 2) and its output names the stopped step and that it stopped twice.
2. Gate stub exits 124 once, then 0: first land exits 4, second lands (exit 0, master moved).
3. Gate stub exits 124, the branch gets a new code commit, gate exits 124 again: exit 4 again (a different code is a fresh first stop).
4. T11 as today: one stop gives exit 4, outcome handed_back, master unchanged.
reason: tests/test_land.py:242, :253, :260 pass; :242 fails on base; t11 still passes.
findings.summary: relay land hands back a stopped gate with no bound: code that hangs a test every time is run again every 30 min forever

details: PLAUSIBLE: traced, not reproduced (T6 passed 16 of 16 runs). The main thread joins the timer only in main()'s finally, which
runs after _run's finally has already called probe.stop(). stop_tree's final SIGKILL covers `set(pids) | set(_descendants(root))`
taken at the end of the grace, so any program the main thread started in the meantime is killed. The window is the time
between the last child's death and the watchdog's last `ps` (tens of ms). Harm is small (a stale worktree entry that git
prunes later), hence LOW.
Size: 10 agent minutes.
evidence: lib/relay_ci.py:485-490 (_stop_at_limit -> stop_tree), lib/relay_ci.py:114-124 (stop_tree: final kill of _descendants(root)),
lib/relay_ci.py _run finally: self.probe.stop() before main()'s timer.join().
failing_case: A quick gate under relay gate stops at the limit while every child dies at SIGTERM at once: the main thread's step returns,
_LimitStop runs Probe.stop, which starts `git worktree remove --force` and `git worktree prune`; the watchdog thread, its grace
loop just ended, lists `_descendants(me)` and SIGKILLs that git. Now (when the timing meets): the probe's .git/worktrees entry
is left (the folder is then removed by rmtree, the record file too), a stale prunable worktree in the repository. Should: the
cleanup starts only after the watchdog's kills are done.
fix_hint: Set a threading.Event at the end of _stop_at_limit and wait on it in step() before raising _LimitStop (or join the timer
there), so Probe.stop and every later program start after the watchdog is done.
pass_cases: 1. T6 as today, and `git worktree list --porcelain` shows only the main worktree with no "prunable" line, over 20 runs.
2. A stop where the probe ignores SIGTERM for 1 s: the probe worktree is still removed and no prunable entry is left.
reason: tests/test_ci_python.py:525 passes and fails on base.
findings.summary: after a stop the main thread cleans the probe while the watchdog may still SIGKILL every descendant, its git worktree remove included

Size: 5 agent minutes (front, relay queue note).
evidence: $ bin/relay queue show speed-up-the-quick-gate | grep -n "1500\|25 после\|QUICK_LIMIT"   (no output)
